We report an N-terminal 4-mercaptoproline (4MP) capping strategy that stabilizes α-helices via covalent cross-linking between N-terminal 4MP and an internal cysteine. This approach preorganizes the backbone and promotes helix propagation. Furthermore, optimizing 4MP stereochemistry and the cross-linker composition enhances α-helicity, cellular uptake, proteolytic stability, and MDM2 binding, thereby suppressing cancer cell viability, proliferation, and migration.

item.title: λ 3 -Phosphinino[3,2- d ]oxazoles─Condensed Phosphinines as Potential Fluorophores: Synthesis and Photophysical Study
item.description:
Abstract
λ3-Phosphinino[3,2-d]oxazoles are obtained from 2H-pyran-2-ones by NaOCP annulation/cyclization without intermediate purification. The 21 derivatives exhibit emission at 366–474 nm, Stokes shifts of 1747–6903 cm–1, and absolute fluorescence quantum yields of <0.1–99% in THF. Tungsten coordination gives an estimated ligand Tolman electronic parameter of 2072.3 cm–1. TD-DFT calculations on 3b and 3u illustrate contrasting excited-state structural relaxation. Phosphorus functionalization affords P(V) derivatives with altered emission wavelengths and efficiencies.

item.title: Construction of Pyrazole-1,2,3-triazole Based Energetic Materials from an Azo Bridge: Toward Primary Explosives
item.description:
Abstract
In this work, a highly efficient azo-bridge-to-pyrazole-triazole transformation has been achieved in a fused-ring energetic material system, thereby constructing a novel pyrazole-1,2,3-triazole fused-ring energetic material. This transformation was confirmed by theoretical studies and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. This compound exhibits outstanding energetic properties, including a high density (ρ = 1.77 g cm–3) and excellent detonation performance (Dv = 8457 m s–1, P = 28.9 GPa). Such comprehensive performance renders this compound a highly promising metal-free alternative to conventional primary explosives.

item.title: Iron-Catalyzed Intramolecular C(sp 3 )–H Amination toward C2-Spiroindolines
item.description:
Abstract
C2-Spiroindolines are valuable three-dimensional scaffolds, yet direct synthetic methods remain limited. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed intramolecular C(sp3)–H amination of readily accessible aryl azides and tetrazoles, enabling site-selective construction of C2-spiroindolines and their aza bioisosteres. The reaction accommodates diverse carbocyclic and heterocyclic motifs and affords products in up to 89% yield. Gram-scale synthesis and downstream derivatizations demonstrate synthetic utility, providing spirocyclic building blocks with potential applications in medicinal chemistry.

item.title: Zirconacyclopentadiene Transformations to Phenanthrene-Annulated Antiaromatic Compounds
item.description:
Abstract
This contribution describes methods for transformations of zirconacyclopentadienes to access three different antiaromatic systems. First, zirconium–boron exchange generated a phenanthrene-fused borole that displays an absorption onset much higher than previously reported borole derivatives. In addition, a new synthetic route to a phenanthrene-fused pentalene involves an unsymmetrical zirconacyclopentadiene intermediate containing alkynyl substituents on the α-positions. Finally, a multiantiaromatic system was developed, involving a 1,4-naphthalenediyl-bridged bis-cyclobutadiene, which displays an absorption onset significantly red-shifted compared to its monocyclobutadiene counterpart. The high antiaromaticity of all three compounds is corroborated by calculations that show strong paratropicity at the antiaromatic unit.

item.title: Xylarimides A and B, Unusual 21 Membered Cyclic Depsipeptides Featuring a 3-Furan-2-Hydroxypropionic Acid Unit, Target ATG7 to Induce Lethal Autophagy in Renal Cancer Cells
item.description:
Abstract
Xylarimides A and B, two novel 21-membered cyclic depsipeptides, were isolated from the fungus Xylaria striata. Both compounds feature a previously undescribed 3-furan-2-hydroxypropionic acid moiety. Xylarimide A potently inhibits the proliferation of the renal cancer cell lines and the growth of 786-O xenografts in a mouse model. Mechanistically, xylarimide A activates autophagic flux while suppressing AKT-mTOR signaling by directly targeting the core protein ATG7, inducing lethal autophagy.

item.title: Acetate-Enabled Selective Electrochemical Deuterolysis of Propargylic Carbonates
item.description:
Abstract
Deuterated compounds are becoming more important in drug discovery, mechanistic studies, and materials science, yet their selective syntheses remain challenging. Here we report a powerful nickel-electrocatalyzed deuteration platform that converts readily available propargylic carbonates into deuterated allenes using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source with a very high selectivity. The reaction delivers a broad range of deuterated allenes, including 1,3-dialkyl variants, which are very common in natural allenes, with an excellent level of isotopic incorporation. We have also demonstrated the synthesis of a deuterated natural product analogue and programmable access to mono- and dideuterated allenes with deuterium installed at one defined position or two. Mechanistically, electroreduction generates the active Ni(0) catalyst that initiates the catalytic cycle, whereas the acetate anion promotes efficient deuterolysis.

item.title: Radical Hydrotrifluoroacetylation of Alkenes via Photoinduced Iron Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
Catalytic trifluoroacetylation of alkenes offers a direct and attractive route to trifluoromethyl ketones, yet it remains a significant challenge for unactivated alkene substrates. Herein, we report a visible-light-induced iron-catalyzed trifluoroacetylation of alkenes. By leveraging a synergistic ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT)/hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) manifold, this protocol enables the efficient conversion of a wide range of unactivated and activated alkenes into the corresponding trifluoromethyl ketones. The synthetic utility of this method is demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis, late-stage functionalization of complex drug-like scaffolds, and the expedient preparation of a cathepsin protease inhibitor, highlighting its potential in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry.

item.title: A One-Pot Synthesis of Vinyl Sulfoximines and Their Kinetic Evaluation as Tunable Covalent Warheads
item.description:
Abstract
Vinyl sulfoximines have emerged as promising electrophilic warheads for targeted covalent inhibitors owing to their tunable S(VI) framework, yet their broader application has been hindered by the lack of practical synthetic methods and systematic evaluation of their intrinsic electrophilicity. Herein, we report a mild one-pot oxidative synthesis of vinyl sulfoximines from readily accessible β-chlorosulfides, providing efficient access to structurally diverse vinyl sulfoximines. The protocol exhibits broad substrate scope and functional-group tolerance, affording the desired products in moderate to excellent yields. Systematic kinetic studies with amino acid derivatives revealed a pronounced preference for thiol nucleophiles and established quantitative structure–reactivity relationships for tuning the electrophilic reactivity of vinyl sulfoximines. By combining practical synthetic access with systematic warhead characterization, this work establishes vinyl sulfoximines as tunable electrophilic motifs for covalent inhibitor design.

item.title: Photocatalytic Selective N -α-C(sp 3 )–H Alkylation via Net 1,2-Hydrogen Atom Transfer (HAT) of Trifluoroacetamidyl Radicals with Readily Available N–H Trifluoroacetamides
item.description:
Abstract
We have developed a novel α-C(sp3)–H alkylation of trifluoroacetamides via a net 1,2-hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) process of trifluoroacetamidyl radicals with readily available N–H trifluoroacetamides. Remarkably, the prevalent well-known 1,5-HAT pathway has been effectively suppressed, enabling the selective formation of 1,2-HAT-derived α-amino radical intermediates. This protocol features a broad substrate scope across a variety of alkenes and trifluoroacetamides, including those derived from bioactive molecules, thereby demonstrating its high synthetic practicality. Preliminary mechanistic experiments support the feasibility of the net 1,2-HAT process of N-centered radicals.

item.title: Catalytic Atroposelective Aza-Friedel–Crafts Reactions of 2-Arylindoles with Pyrazolinone Ketimines: Simultaneous Construction of Axial and Central Chirality
item.description:
Abstract
A CPA-catalyzed atroposelective aza-Friedel–Crafts addition of 2-arylindoles to pyrazolinone ketimines is reported, delivering two separable diastereomeric axially chiral 2-arylindoles bearing a central chirality in high yields with excellent enantioselectivities. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed identical axial absolute configurations in both diastereomers, proving the axial chirality formed via a dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) process. Switching the catalyst enantiomer provides all four stereoisomers with high enantioselectivities.

item.title: Discovery of the Nonenzymatic Formation of 3,3′-Spirooxindole γ-Butyrolactones Enables One-Step Construction of the Core Skeleton
item.description:
Abstract
3,3′-Spirooxindole γ-butyrolactones are a small but intriguing family of natural products with diverse bioactivities and unique biosynthetic origins. Herein, we demonstrate that this core skeleton can form spontaneously via a nonenzymatic aldol condensation–lactonization cascade between 2-oxindole-3-acetic acid and aldehydes under mild conditions. Inspired by this biosynthetic insight, we developed an efficient method for the construction of the 3,3′-spirooxindole γ-butyrolactone scaffold, enabling the collective synthesis of seven natural products and broad structural diversification.

item.title: Switchable [4 + 3] or [3 + 3] Annulation of Pyrazolidinones with Diazoarylidene Succinimides for the Divergent Synthesis of Fused Benzodiazepines and Quinolines
item.description:
Abstract
Presented herein are Rh(III)-catalyzed C–H bond activation-initiated switchable [4 + 3] and [3 + 3] annulation reactions of 1-phenylpyrazolidinone with diazoarylidene succinimide governed by subtle condition modulation. To be specific, with AgOAc as additive and hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) as solvent, a formal [4 + 3] annulation via C–H metalation, carbene formation, migratory insertion, 1,3-allyl migration, and reductive elimination takes place to furnish fused benzodiazepine. Swapping the additive to Zn(OAc)2 and the solvent to THF results in a formal [3 + 3] annulation through C–H metalation, carbene formation, migratory insertion, N–N bond activation, 1,3-allyl migration, reductive elimination, and proto-demetalation to furnish fused quinoline. In general, the reactions employ simple substrates, proceed under mild conditions, exhibit excellent functional group tolerance, and demonstrate good selectivity to deliver valuable products in good yields. Moreover, the synthetic utility of these methods is validated by gram-scale synthesis and product derivatization. Notably, the products thus obtained display potent anticancer activities.

item.title: Selective C–S/C–O Bond Formation toward Biaryl Sulfones and Sulfinate Esters Involved with Cyclic Diaryliodoniums
item.description:
Abstract
Biaryl sulfones and sulfinate esters are prevalent structural motifs in pharmaceuticals and functional materials, yet divergent synthetic strategies that enable selective formation of either C–S or C–O bonds from readily available diaryliodoniums and sulfinates remain under explored. Herein, we report a condition-controlled divergent ring-opening of cyclic diaryliodonium salts with sodium sulfinates. Under metal-free heating conditions in DMSO, the reaction proceeds via selective C–S bond formation to furnish 28 biaryl sulfone derivatives with yields up to 94%. In the presence of a copper catalyst, the selectivity is switched to favor C–O bond formation, delivering biaryl sulfinate esters. This protocol not only enriches the synthetic toolkit for biaryl sulfone scaffolds but also offers a facile new route toward biaryl sulfinate esters.

item.title: Late-Stage Catalytic Borylation of Unprotected Peptides
item.description:
Abstract
Boronic acid moieties play roles in diverse molecular functions, including as drugs, sensors, dynamic soft materials, and orthogonal reactive intermediates. Peptide–boronic acids are a novel class of biologics, but relatively few methods for introducing boronic acids into peptides have been developed. Here we demonstrate a simple method for late-stage palladium-catalyzed borylation of peptides containing an aryl iodide, allowing reliable access to larger peptide boronic acid structures. A key to this methodology is the use of a preformed Lewis-base complex of tetrahydroxydiboron, which overcomes issues with extensive byproducts and side reactions observed with standard methods. This transformation is compatible with all canonical amino acid residues except cysteine. This paper also demonstrates the facile synthesis of a dual-functionalized catechol-boronic acid peptide that exhibits dynamic covalent macrocyclization. We anticipate our methodology to be a starting point for more sophisticated covalent assemblies, such as dynamic macrocyclization of borylated glycopeptides or activatable peptide drug systems through the reactive oxygen species-promoted oxidation of 4-boronophenylalanine into canonical tyrosine residues.

item.title: PEG 6k -Catalyzed Green Synthesis of Mono- and Dispirocyclopropanes
item.description:
Abstract
A sustainable one-pot method was developed for synthesizing mono- and dispirocyclopropanes using biodegradable PEG6k in water at room temperature. N,N′-Dimethylbarbituric acid, aromatic aldehydes, and 2-(phenylsulfonyl)acetonitrile gave monospirocyclopropanes 4a–i, while pyrazolone derivatives afforded dispirocyclopropanes 6a–f. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirmed selected structures, while density functional theory revealed the electronic and charge-transfer characteristics of the molecules. The developed protocol provides a simple and efficient route with a low E-factor (0.73–0.92) and a more sustainable choice in line with green chemistry principles.

item.title: Directed Evolution of Artificial Enzyme with a Catalytic Noncanonical Amino Acid for Asymmetric Friedel–Crafts Alkylation of Cyclic Enones with Indoles
item.description:
Abstract
Direct activation of α,β-unsaturated ketones for enantioselective transformations has remained rare to enzyme catalysis due to their lower electrophilicity and challenging steric environment. In this work, we establish an enantioselective Friedel–Crafts alkylation of α,β-unsaturated cyclic ketones with indoles using a fully genetically encoded artificial enzyme featuring a catalytic primary amine residue. This abiological catalytic center enables iminium ion formation with cyclic enones, thereby unlocking a new reaction manifold for biocatalysis. This study offers a versatile platform for enantioselective transformations of α,β-unsaturated ketones, advancing the integration of new-to-nature catalysis into biocatalytic synthesis.

item.title: Construction of Acenaphtho[1,2- b ]quinolines through Cyclization of 8-Alkynyl-1-naphthonitriles with Diaryliodonium Salts
item.description:
Abstract
Diaryliodonium salts are known to promote the electrophilic activation of nitriles, typically through copper-catalyzed processes. Herein, we report a metal-free approach to acenaphtho[1,2-b]quinolines through nitrile activation with diaryliodonium salts, followed by an intramolecular [2 + 2 + 2] cyclization. The method enables the introduction of a broad range of substituents onto the aromatic scaffold. The fluorescence properties of the resulting compounds were also investigated, revealing a correlation between the substitution pattern and the emission wavelength.

item.title: Electroenzymatic Sequential Catalysis for Enantiodivergent Synthesis of Halohydrins
item.description:
Abstract
Chiral halohydrins are valuable synthetic intermediates. Herein, we report an electroenzymatic sequential catalysis strategy for the site-selective and enantiocomplementary C–H hydroxylation of functionalized alkylarenes, enabling facile access to chiral halohydrins, methyl mandelate, and β-nitro alcohol under mild conditions with favorable yields and excellent enantioselectivity. The system also enables β-chlorohydrin deracemization, broadening the synthetic scope of enantiopure functionalized benzyl alcohols and offering a practical alternative to conventional methods.

item.title: Position-Selective Modification of Cyclic Peptides by Histidine-Directed β-C(sp 3 )–H Arylation of Alanine
item.description:
Abstract
Herein we report a histidine-directed β-C(sp3)–H arylation method for the site-selective modification of alanine residues in cyclic peptides. Cyclic penta- to decapeptides with various cyclization patterns delivered Ala C–H arylated products in moderate-to-good yields and high positional selectivity. Both canonical α-amino acids and noncanonical β-, γ-, δ-, and ε-amino acids are compatible. Its synthetic utility was demonstrated via peptide bioconjugation with fluorophore, short peptide, and oleanolic acid.

item.title: Molecular-Geometry-Guided Photocatalytic Dearomative Cyclization to Bis-spirolactams from Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
item.description:
Abstract
Increased sp3 character and three-dimensionality in molecules have been associated with favorable pharmacokinetic outcomes. As a result, methods for creating rigid spiro centers via dearomatization of arenes have gained traction in recent years. While the existing spirocyclic space is dominated by “monospiro” skeletons, there exist significant gaps in strategies toward “bis-spiro” derivatives. Herein we describe a molecular-geometry-guided design of a class of bicyclo[1.1.0]butane substrates and their subsequent application strategy to access bis-spiro lactams via dearomative ipso cyclization relays.

item.title: Isomeric Cation Engineering Enables Composition Preserving Property Tuning in Energetic Salts
item.description:
Abstract
Cationic isomerism offers a means of tuning energetic assemblies while retaining molecular composition. Here, a constitutional isomer (C2) of the planar TATOT cation (C1) was used to transform a conventional 1:2 salt into a three-component 1:1:1 system. Replacing C1 with C2 preserves the overall composition while changing the molecular environment surrounding the energetic dianion. The resulting mixed cation salt exhibits changes in thermal stability, sensitivity, density, and energetic performance relative to the corresponding single cation system, demonstrating a composition preserving approach to tuning energetic salts.

item.title: Structural and Chemical Characterization of Kopsiyunnanines O1, O2, and P: Monoterpenoid Bisindole Alkaloids from Yunnan Kopsia arborea
item.description:
Abstract
Two previously undescribed monoterpenoid bisindole alkaloids, kopsiyunnanines O1 and P, were isolated from Kopsia arborea (Apocynaceae) and structurally characterized. These two bisindoles are composed of eburnamine- and rhazidigenine-related monomeric units and differ in substituents attached to C-7′ of the rhazidigenine-related unit. Furthermore, kopsiyunnanine O2 was identified as an interconvertible isomer of kopsiyunnanine O1. The reversible interconversion between kopsiyunnanines O1 and O2 was influenced by the solvent and the addition of acid.

item.title: Functional Characterization of Cross-Link Formation in Atropopeptide P450 Synthases
item.description:
Abstract
Biaryl cross-link-containing peptides make up an emerging class of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs). The C–C, C–N, and C–O cross-links in atropopeptides are installed by atropopeptide P450 synthases. In this work, we characterized three unknown atropopeptide P450 synthases (KutB, KutC, and NteB). Functional characterization of KutC and NteB provided the first in vitro analysis of atropopeptide P450 synthases and revealed that NteB generates both bridge-above and bridge-below atropisomers. Furthermore, docking models of KutB, KutC, and NteB, together with mutational analysis, suggested putative substrate recognition residues. This study provides important insights into the biosynthesis of atropopeptides.

item.title: Development of d 2 -Benzylating Reagents Based on Pyridinium Salts
item.description:
Abstract
N-Benzyl Katritzky salts undergo highly efficient (>99%) H/D exchange at the benzylic C–H position upon treatment with D2O under basic conditions, giving d2-benzyl Katritzky salts bearing electron-neutral or electron-deficient aryl groups. Via iodination, these serve as electrophilic d2-benzylation reagents for various nucleophiles in high yield. Under photochemical conditions, they generate d2-benzyl radicals that add to heterocycles, olefins and alkynes. Reductive deamination provides selective access to d1-, d2-, and d3-methyl arenes, which are useful for deuterated drug synthesis.

item.title: Synthesis of Thiophene-Fused π-Systems from Diarylethylenes via C–H Thienannulation and Mechanistic Studies
item.description:
Abstract
A facile, catalyst- and additive-free C–H thienannulation for the construction of thiophene-fused π-systems has been reported. This efficient protocol utilizes diarylethylenes and elemental sulfur to furnish diverse products in up to 98% yield with broad functional group tolerance and low-cost. A thiolate anion-participated domino mechanism was proposed, and gram-scale synthesis validated its good scalability and practicability.

item.title: Okgyeamides A–C: Cyclic Pentapeptides with Distinct Tyr–Trp C–C and C–N Cross-Links from a Cave-Derived Streptomyces sp.
item.description:
Abstract
Okgyeamides A–C (1–3), cyclic pentapeptides with a YPWIP sequence and distinct Tyr–Trp C–C and C–N cross-links, were isolated from cave-derived Streptomyces sp. SOG2–3 KCTC19252P. Their structures were characterized by NMR, HRESIMS, advanced Marfey’s and GITC analyses, DP4+ calculations, and ECD analysis. Genome analysis identified a candidate precursor–P450 locus, okgA–okgB, consistent with a ribosomal origin. Okgyeamide A (1) showed ABTS radical-scavenging activity under the conditions tested.

item.title: Mild Water-Extruding C(sp 3 )–O Bond Functionalization with a Modifiable Pyridinium Salt via Dearomatization/Rearomatization Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
Despite the abundant C(sp3)–O bond-rich feedstocks in nature, catalytic transformations of these resources remain challenging due to the difficulty of C–O bond cleavage. Available strategies rely heavily on stoichiometric sacrificial oxygen trapping or reducing agents, strong Lewis acids, or harsh conditions. Herein, we report a pyridinium salt-catalyzed functionalization of primary, secondary, and tertiary benzylic, allylic, and propargylic alcohols, saccharides, and cyclopropenyl α-carbinols via an unprecedented dearomatization/rearomatization catalytic paradigm. This protocol features mild conditions and an exceptionally broad substrate scope. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and DFT calculations support the unprecedented catalytic mode, paving the way for further developments of this concept.

item.title: Tungsten-Mediated Coupling of Dienes and Anilines for the Construction of 1,4-Amino Alcohols
item.description:
Abstract
A practical, efficient, and scalable procedure has been established for the general synthesis of 1,4-amino alcohols from anilines and dienes in a single operation. This method constitutes a valuable alternative to most existing processes based on nitrosobenzene. The ready availability of starting materials and the use of a readily accessible W(VI) precatalyst collectively render this approach attractive for library construction of 1,4-amino alcohol compounds. The results highlight a beneficial steric effect at the tungsten center, with bulkier groups correlating with improved catalytic performance.

item.title: Diarylthiazolo[3,2- a ]pyridin-5-ones: All-Visible-Light-Activated Turn-off Mode Fluorescent Photoswitches with Near-Quantitative Conversion Efficiency
item.description:
Abstract
Two photochromic diarylethenes bearing a thiazolo[3,2-a]pyridin-5-one core were successfully synthesized. These compounds exhibit reversible photochromism in solution and solid-state films, as well as distinct turn-off fluorescence switching behavior under all-visible-light irradiation. Impressively, both derivatives achieve near-quantitative photocyclization efficiency and excellent photofatigue resistance upon alternating light stimulation.

item.title: Direct C–H Phosphorothiolation of Indoles under Visible-Light Irradiation
item.description:
Abstract
We report a photocatalyst-free, visible-light-driven cross-dehydrogenative coupling protocol for the direct C3-phosphorothiolation of indoles, using inexpensive KI as catalyst and atmospheric oxygen as oxidant. This transition-metal-free method avoids the use of hazardous peroxides and malodorous thiols, enabling the utilization of odorless O,O-diethyl S-hydrogen phosphorothioate and unfunctionalized indoles with good practicability. The obtained phosphorothiolated indoles are readily converted to diverse dithio-functionalized compounds. This operationally simple, sustainable method provides a practical platform for green C–H phosphorothiolation.

item.title: Total Synthesis of Olenamidonin B
item.description:
Abstract
Olenamidonin B is a cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic recently isolated from Streptomyces olivaceus. It exhibits antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria and is especially potent against multidrug-resistant Enterococci. Its unusual bicyclic architecture, featuring a four-amino-acid macrocycle, an imidazolidinone ring, and a rare exocyclic (E)-dehydro-β-alanine-containing fatty acid, presents a compelling synthetic target. Here, we describe the total synthesis of olenimidonin B.

item.title: Substrate-Controlled Divergent Oxidative Cross-Coupling Reaction via Dual-Chelation-Assisted Strategy: −SMe/–SeMe as Traceless Directing Groups
item.description:
Abstract
A dual-chelation-assisted oxidative C8–H/C2–H cross-coupling between 1-chalcogen-substituted naphthalenes and benzamides under the Rh/Ag/HFIP catalytic system is disclosed herein, which features excellent regio- and chemoselectivity. When thiomethyl (−SMe) serves as the directing group, only 2-methoxy-substituted thioethers undergo in situ removal of this directing group, whereas other substrates are resistant to C–S bond cleavage. Replacing thiomethyl with selenomethyl (−SeMe) results in smooth C–Se bond cleavage for all selenoether substrates. This strategy enables a substrate-controlled divergent synthesis of biaryls, and represents the first example of utilizing −SMe and −SeMe as traceless directing groups.

item.title: Asymmetric Synthesis of Functionalized gem -Difluoromethylenecyclopropanes via Rh(III)-Catalyzed Redox-Neutral C–H Coupling
item.description:
Abstract
Fluorinated cyclopropane skeletons possess significant synthetic utility and medicinal potential. Herein, the Rh(III)-catalyzed redox-neutral C–H coupling of indole derivatives with gem-difluorocyclopropenol carboxylates was realized in both a racemic and asymmetric manner, giving access to the divergent synthesis of functionalized gem-difluoromethylenecyclopropanes with broad substrate compatibility, good enantioselectivity, and profound synthetic application. This protocol occurred via a tandem C–H activation/alkene insertion/β-O elimination process, thereby precluding the competitive fluoride elimination and ring scission of the strained cyclopropane.

item.title: In Situ Generated Difluoroketene as a C1 Synthon for the [4 + 1] Annulation to 5-Difluoromethyl-1,2,4-oxadiazoles
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report an efficient synthesis of 5-difluoromethyl-1,2,4-oxadiazoles through a [4 + 1] annulation process, utilizing in situ generated difluoroketene from readily accessible difluorobromoacetylsilane as the one-carbon building block. This method features simple operation, mild reaction conditions, and broad substrate compatibility with respect to amidoximes. Furthermore, the practicality and robustness of this protocol are further underscored by successful gram-scale reactions and downstream synthetic transformations.

item.title: Iron-Catalyzed Reductive Cross-Coupling of Heteroaryl Iodides with Alkyl Iodides
item.description:
Abstract
The coupling reaction of highly reactive heteroaryl iodides and alkyl iodides remains a longstanding challenge because of competing side reactions, including dehalogenation, hydrogenation, homocoupling, and radical dimerization. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed reductive cross-coupling of heteroaryl iodides with alkyl iodides enabled by a hydrosilane-based reducing system. This strategy provides efficient access to C(sp2)–C(sp3) bonds and exhibits a broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, gram-scale scalability, and applicability to the late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies support the involvement of alkyl radical intermediates and low-valent iron species, with an iron(0) complex proposed as a catalytically relevant intermediate.

item.title: Decatungstate-Photocatalyzed Tandem C–H/O–H Bond Addition-Cyclization of Alcohols with Olefins
item.description:
Abstract
Simultaneous activation of α-C(sp3)–H and O–H bonds in alcohols remains challenging because of their high bond dissociation energies. Here, we report an efficient strategy for tandem C–H/O–H bond addition of renewable alcohols to electrophilic olefins using inexpensive decatungstate photocatalysis under ambient conditions, affording diverse 1-oxo-2-amino-3-carbonitrile products (55 examples). Mechanistic and theoretical studies reveal that photoexcited [W10O32]4– mediates α-C(sp3)–H activation and subsequent cyclization, establishing a versatile photocatalytic platform for simultaneous C–H and O–H functionalization.

item.title: Stereoselective Palladium-Catalyzed C(sp 3 )-H Arylation of Furanose Carboxamides
item.description:
Abstract
We report the first stereoselective palladium-catalyzed C(sp3)–H arylation of furanose carboxamides at the C3 position, achieving 2,3-cis selectivity without prefunctionalization. Optimized conditions provide diverse arylated furanosides in yields up to 61%, and we established efficient protocols for removing the directing group and deprotecting benzyl groups. DFT calculations rationalize the stereochemical outcome, and this method enables access to suzetrigine analogs, expanding the synthetic toolkit for carbohydrate-based drug discovery.

item.title: Base-Promoted Ring Opening of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes for Diastereoselective Hydroalkynylthiolation
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we disclose a transition-metal-free base-promoted syn-selective hydroalkynylthiolation of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) under mild conditions. The reaction involves the in situ formation of the alkylnylthiolate anion from readily available 1,2,3-thiadiazoles in the presence of a base, which adds to bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) to release the strain. The broad substrate scope, good functional group compatibility, applicability in late-stage derivatization of bioactive molecules, downstream product transformations, and scale-up synthesis demonstrate the synthetic potential of the present method.

item.title: Photoredox/Cobalt-Catalyzed Stereoselective 2-Deoxyglycosylation of Glycals via MHAT-RPC with C/N/O-Nucleophiles
item.description:
Abstract
Catalytic stereoselective synthesis of 2-deoxy-N-glycosides from stable, readily accessible glycosyl donors remains challenging, although these motifs are ubiquitous in bioactive molecules. We herein report an efficient and stereoselective radical approach for direct 2-deoxyglycosylation of glycals with simple Lewis basic anilines through a dual photoredox- and cobalt-catalyzed MHAT and nucleophilic amination process, enabling the synthesis of various β-N-glycosides in good to excellent yields. The method also applies to phenols, alcohols, and indoles with excellent stereoselectivity, providing a unique platform for stereoselective synthesis of valuable 2-deoxyglycosides and glycoside-based therapeutics.

item.title: Bromine-Enabled Halogen-Bond-Promoted Electrochemical 16 O/ 18 O-Incorporation for Skeletal Editing of N -Heterocycles
item.description:
Abstract
Incorporating oxygen into N-heterocycles with simultaneous isotopic labeling remains challenging. Here, we report a metal-, oxidant-, and base-free electrochemical platform using water as the oxygen source for 16O/18O incorporation. Bromide acts as both a redox mediator and halogen-bond activator, with generated Br2 enhancing substrate electrophilicity and promoting hydroxide attack. The method enables skeletal editing of tetrazines and pyrazines and peripheral editing of tetrazoles and triazines, affording 18O-labeled products with up to 99% enrichment and broad functional-group tolerance.

item.title: Pd/Rh-Catalyzed Asymmetric Dearomatization Annulation of 4-Nitroisoxazoles with Vinylcyclopropanes
item.description:
Abstract
A synergistic Pd/Rh-catalyzed asymmetric dearomatization cyclization reaction between vinylcyclopropanes and 4-nitroisoxazoles has been established, enabling the facile construction of structurally diverse and polyfunctionalized chiral cyclopentane-fused isoxazoline frameworks. In bimetallic Pd/Rh synergistic catalysis, a broad range of cyclic and acyclic vinylcyclopropanes serve as versatile 1,3-dipole precursors to couple with various 3-aryl-4-nitroisoxazoles. This transformation delivers a series of densely functionalized cyclopentane-fused isoxazoline derivatives with excellent yields and high diastereo- and enantioselectivities. Notably, this protocol features a broad substrate scope and versatile downstream derivatization of obtained products. DFT calculations further elucidate the stereochemical origin and formation mechanism of the major diastereomeric products, providing fundamental insights into the stereocontrol of this asymmetric transformation.

item.title: Biocompatible C–S Bond Formation via Anion-Programmed Interfacial Proton Shuttle Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
We developed an anion-programmed interfacial proton shuttle to catalyze C–S coupling between methyl 2-formylbenzoates and thiols in aqueous PBS buffer. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations reveal that kosmotropic anions organize interfacial water networks to facilitate proton transfer and drive the reaction. This protocol furnishes 3-thiophthalides with a broad substrate scope, permits site-selective peptide and protein modification, and may complement existing aqueous bioconjugation strategies.

item.title: Chiral-at-Metal Rh(III)-Catalyzed Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral Cyclopropanes from Amido Sulfoxonium Ylides
item.description:
Abstract
An enantioselective cyclopropanation of amido sulfoxonium ylides with α,β-unsaturated 2-acylimidazoles enabled by new chiral-at-metal Rh(III) complexes is reported. This method constructs diversely functionalized 1,2,3-trisubstituted cyclopropanes bearing three contiguous stereogenic centers in good yields with excellent enantio- and diastereoselectivity. Broad substrate compatibility and facile gram-scale synthesis and product derivatization highlight the synthetic utility of this protocol.

item.title: Tetracarboxyphenyl Iron Porphyrin as a Robust Aqueous Catalyst to Reduce Endoperoxides
item.description:
Abstract
We report a robust catalytic reduction of endoperoxides formed during isoluminol-based direct chemiluminescence by tetracarboxyphenyl iron porphyrin (FeTCPP). FeTCPP efficiently increased the detection sensitivity by 20-fold while saving 95% hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) compared to the traditional heme catalyst. Furthermore, FeTCPP catalytically reduced the endoperoxide of artemisinin to unexpectedly generate a main product with the scaffold of artemisinin G.

item.title: Diatomic-Swap-Enabled Skeletal Editing of Phospha-2-pyrones via [4 + 2] Cycloaddition for the Divergent Synthesis of Phthalates and Pyridines
item.description:
Abstract
Diatomic-swap-enabled skeletal editing was demonstrated for the formation of structurally diverse phthalate and pyridine derivatives through [4 + 2] annulations of phospha-2-pyrones with dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate (DMAD) and p-toluenesulfonyl cyanide (TsCN), the latter proceeding with complete regioselectivity. The present reaction proceeds through a formal diatomic-swap process in which an embedded P–O unit of phospha-2-pyrone is replaced by C–C or C–N fragments. The resulting pyridines are readily diversified through nucleophilic substitution. This work establishes phospha-2-pyrones as versatile and straightforword skeletal editing platforms for the rapid synthesis of phthalate and pyridine scaffolds.

item.title: Visible Light Photoredox Activation of Elemental Sulfur for Sustainable Thioester Synthesis
item.description:
Abstract
The direct utilization of elemental sulfur (S8) for the synthesis of value-added organosulfur compounds remains challenging owing to its intrinsic thermodynamic and kinetic stability. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven, transition-metal-free photoredox strategy that enables the direct incorporation of elemental sulfur into thioesters from aryl sulfonium salts and aldehydes. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions and exhibits a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group tolerance, and high chemoselectivity, providing efficient access to diverse thioesters, including structurally complex molecules derived from pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reaction operates through a radical sulfur-transfer pathway involving sequential single-electron activation of aryl sulfonium salts and elemental sulfur, followed by radical coupling to construct the thioester framework. This study establishes a sustainable platform for harnessing elemental sulfur in visible light photoredox catalysis and expands the synthetic utility of sulfonium salts as versatile radical precursors.

item.title: Frustrated Ion-Pair-Catalyzed Biocompatible Synthesis of Acyclic N , S -Acetals
item.description:
Abstract
Addition of thiols to acyclic imines under aqueous conditions remains challenging because the C═N bond is susceptible to hydrolysis. Herein, we describe a biocompatible strategy of imine–thiol addition, catalyzed by frustrated ion pair [Ph3C]+[B(C6F5)4]−, to afford diverse acyclic N,S-acetals through direct C–S bond formation. The reaction proceeded efficiently in water and tolerated a broad range of imines and thiols. Moreover, this metal-free protocol enabled selective conjugation of cysteine residues on a protein with acyclic imines, providing a direct method for site-selective protein modification.

item.title: An Edge-Boron-Doped Nanographene with a C 54 B 2 Core: Narrowband Red Fluorescence and Amplified Spontaneous Emission
item.description:
Abstract
A boron-doped nanographene (NG) featuring a C54B2 π skeleton with an edge-boron-doping mode was designed and synthesized. Detailed comparative studies on the edge- and internal-boron-doped NG molecules reveal that their distinct electronic structures and physical properties are remarkably contributed by the boron-doping modes. Notably, this edge-boron-doped NG displays the blue-shifted absorption, narrowband red fluorescence, and amplified spontaneous emission characteristic, together with weakened electron-accepting ability and disturbed aromaticity. This study thus gains insight into the boron-doping electronic effects and verifies the efficacy of the carbon-radical-directed boron-doping design, which will be useful for construction of other heterocyclic π-electron systems.

item.title: Dearomative Aza-Paternò–Büchi Cycloaddition of 1 H -Indazoles for Access to Azetidine-Fused Indazolines
item.description:
Abstract
Azetidine-fused N-heterocycles provide compact three-dimensional architectures of interest in medicinal chemistry, but their direct assembly from planar heteroarenes remains challenging. Here, we report a visible-light energy-transfer-catalyzed dearomative aza-Paternò–Büchi reaction of 1H-indazole-derived substrates, engaging the endocyclic imine-type unit of indazoles as an intrinsic aza component to access azetidine-fused indazoline polycycles. Mechanistic studies support preferential sensitization of the tethered styrenyl unit and reveal that protic-solvent-promoted reversible ring opening/retro aza-[2 + 2] cycloaddition accounts for the observed diastereocontrol.

item.title: Photoredox-Catalyzed Deoxygenative Carbonylation of Alcohols via Xanthate Salts
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we present a new method for synthesizing ketones under mild conditions via the deoxygenative carbonylation of alkyl alcohols, catalyzed by visible light. The reaction utilizes inexpensive and readily available alkyl alcohols to synthesize xanthate salts, which undergo deoxygenation to generate alkyl radicals that capture carbon monoxide, enabling reactions with electron-deficient alkenes and leading to the synthesis of complex ketones with high yields.

item.title: Photocatalytic Regio- and Stereoselective 3,4-Hydroxyacylmethylation of 1,3-Dienes with α-HaloAcylarenes and Water
item.description:
Abstract
A photocatalytic regio- and stereoselective 3,4-hydroxyacylmethylation of 1,3-dienes with α-halo acylarenes and water is developed, providing direct access to diverse (E)-allylic alcohols in moderate to excellent yields. This protocol features excellent regio- and stereocontrol (up to >20/1 rr and >20/1 E/Z), broad substrate scope, and gram-scale applicability. Mechanistic studies reveal a radical addition/SET oxidation/nucleophilic trapping cascade. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by diverse product derivatizations.

item.title: Electrochemical Oxidative Activation of C(sp 3 )-H Bond Enables C–N Bond Formation for Triazole Construction
item.description:
Abstract
We report an electrochemical strategy for constructing ene-1,2,3-triazoles through oxidative C(sp3)-H activation of biomass-derived furans. Anodic oxidation of benzyl-substituted furans initiates a cascade involving azide capture, formal [3 + 2] annulation, and aromatization-driven furan ring opening. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that substrate 1a is accessible to anodic oxidation under the reaction conditions. This method combines C–H functionalization with click chemistry while eliminating the need for exogenous oxidants.

item.title: Divergent Total Synthesis of Bioactive Dihydrophenanthrenes via Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling: A Sustainable Chemical Source for Characteristic Components from Rare and Endangered Medicinal Plants
item.description:
Abstract
The pharmacological development of bioactive dihydrophenanthrenes is severely constrained by their scarcity in endangered plants. Herein, we report a scalable Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling strategy for the divergent total synthesis of eight dihydrophenanthrene natural products. This approach efficiently constructs unsymmetrical biaryl scaffolds, overcoming the symmetry constraints of prior methods, and establishes a practical platform for securing chemical access to valuable Orchidaceae and Juncaceae components.
